stem: A child has food refusal and dysphagia with rings and furrows seen on oesophagoscopy; what biopsy finding best supports a diagnosis of eosinophilic oesophagitis?

options.text: At least 15 eosinophils per high-power field on oesophageal biopsy, isolated to the oesophagus
Urticaria within 15 minutes of every meal
Immediate improvement after one dose of antihistamine

explanation: Eosinophilic oesophagitis is supported by oesophageal dysfunction plus at least 15 eosinophils per high-power field on oesophageal biopsy, with eosinophilic inflammation isolated to the oesophagus.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because eosinophilic oesophagitis is diagnosed by symptoms of oesophageal dysfunction together with at least 15 eosinophils per high-power field on oesophageal biopsy, with disease confined to the oesophagus.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a stool viral PCR does not form part of the diagnostic criteria for eosinophilic oesophagitis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because urticaria shortly after meals suggests an immediate allergic reaction rather than the biopsy-based diagnosis of eosinophilic oesophagitis.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because anaemia is not the defining biopsy finding for eosinophilic oesophagitis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because rapid response to antihistamine is not used to diagnose eosinophilic oesophagitis.
